files.s: In this file, we model Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory (+ choice) using Lean's underlying type theory, building on the pre-sets defined in `Mathlib/SetTheory/ZFC/PSet.lean`.

h.d: ZFC set. Defined as `PSet` quotiented by `PSet.Equiv`, the extensional equivalence.
Axiom of choice. Proved from Lean's axiom of choice.
The von Neumann ordinal `ω` as a `Set`.
All functions are classically definable.
Predicate that a ZFC set is a subset of `x × y` that can be considered as a ZFC function `x → y`. That is, each member of `x` is related by the ZFC set to exactly one member of `y`.
ZFC set of ZFC functions `x → y`.

files.s: In this file, we define the cardinalities of ZFC sets as `ZFSet.{u} → Cardinal.{u}`.

h.d: `ZFSet.card x` is equal to the cardinality of `x` as a set of `ZFSet`s.
The cardinality of a ZFC set.

files.s: Classes in set theory are usually defined as collections of elements satisfying some property. We model this by defining `ZFClass` as `Set ZFSet`.

h.d: Defined as `Set ZFSet`.
Definite description operator.
The Burali-Forti paradox. Ordinals form a proper class.
The **Burali-Forti paradox**: ordinals form a proper class.
Unlike the other set constructors, the `iota` definite descriptor is a set for any set input, but not constructively so, so there is no associated `Class → Set` function.
An induction principle for sets. If every subset of a class is a member, then the class is universal.

files.s: This file works towards the development of von Neumann ordinals, i.e. transitive sets, well-ordered under `∈`.

h.d: An ordinal is a transitive set, well-ordered under membership.
An ordinal is a transitive set, trichotomous under membership.
An ordinal is a transitive set of ordinals.
An ordinal is a transitive set of transitive sets.
The simplified form of transitivity used within `IsOrdinal` yields an equivalent definition to the standard one.
The union of transitive sets is transitive.

files.s: A pre-set is inductively defined by its indexing type and its members, which are themselves pre-sets.

h.d: Pre-set.
Underlying type of a pre-set.
Underlying family of pre-sets of a pre-set.
Extensional equivalence of pre-sets. Defined inductively.
The von Neumann ordinal `ω` as a `PSet`.
Two pre-sets are equivalent iff they have the same members.

files.t: Ordinal ranks of PSet and ZFSet
files.s: In this file, we define the ordinal ranks of `PSet` and `ZFSet`. These ranks are the same as `WellFounded.rank` over `∈`, but are defined in a way that the universe levels of ranks are the same as the indexing types.

h.d: `ZFSet.rank` is equal to the `WellFounded.rank` over `∈`.
For the rank of `⋃₀ x`, we only have `rank (⋃₀ x) ≤ rank x ≤ rank (⋃₀ x) + 1`. This inequality is split into `rank_sUnion_le` and `le_succ_rank_sUnion`.
The ordinal rank of a pre-set

files.s: This file defines the von Neumann hierarchy of sets `V_ o` for ordinal `o`, which is recursively defined so that `V_ a = ⋃ b < a, powerset (V_ b)`. This stratifies the universal class, in the sense that `⋃ o, V_ o = univ`.

h.d: Every set is in some element of the von Neumann hierarchy.
